root.name: King's Pawn Game: Weber Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d3 d5 3. exd5 c6 4. dxc6 Nxc6

overview: A counter-gambit against the quiet 2.d3: Black plays ...d5, ...c6 and recaptures on c6 with the knight, leaving White a pawn up (White pawns 7, Black 6 in the FEN). Black has an active knight, an open d-file and a lead in development, and hopes to harass the king in the centre. White can simply consolidate with Nf3, Be2/Be3 and castle.

white_ideas.idea: Consolidate with Nf3 and Be2/Be3, castle and keep the extra pawn
Trade queens on the d-file when it favours the extra pawn

black_ideas.idea: Open the d-file and target the king in the centre
Seek to regain the pawn with ...Bc5 and ...Nd4

typical_structures.structure: Black has a lead in development for a pawn

character.notes: Black sacrifices a pawn for rapid development in an open position.

gambit.notes: In the FEN Black has six pawns to White's seven, and White can hold the extra one.

soundness.notes: Probably dubious for Black, since White's d3 set-up is solid.

structure.notes: Central pawns have come off, so the game is mostly open lines.

level.notes: Easy to learn but not a sound repertoire choice.

character.reason: Black plays a pawn down for activity and the open lines give tactical chances.

gambit.reason: Black has given a pawn that White can keep.

soundness.reason: White can consolidate the extra pawn with natural development.

structure.reason: The central pawns have come off and the game is about open lines for the pieces.

approach.reason: A countergambit against 2.d3 that strong players hardly ever try.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner and White must still play accurately.

plans.reason: Black is pawn-down and relies on quick development.
